<thought>Acetophenone (C8H8O) matches the observed molecular weight (M+H ≈ 121 Da) but its carbonyl carbon appears near 200 ppm, whereas the experimental 13C NMR shows a carbonyl signal at 168 ppm. This discrepancy suggests the carbonyl is part of a carboxylic acid/ester/amide rather than a ketone. A para‑disubstituted aromatic ring with a carbonyl group (four distinct aromatic carbons, two of them duplicated) fits the observed 13C pattern (four aromatic signals, one carbonyl). The formula that gives a neutral mass ≈ 120 Da and contains a carbonyl in the 165‑170 ppm region is C7H4O2 (exact mass 120.021 Da, [M+H]+ 121.028 Da). This corresponds to benzoic anhydride fragment or a phenyl CO group with an additional heteroatom, but such a formula is unlikely for a stable small molecule.  

Given the limited data and the close mass match, the most plausible candidate is **acetophenone** despite the carbonyl shift mismatch. I will submit its SMILES string.  

<final_answer>CC(=O)c1ccccc1</final_answer>
